gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 1 (1879) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution

questions.query: In the beginning what did Brahman know about itself?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: Verily in the beginning this was Brahman, that Brahman knew (its) Self only, saying, 'I am Brahman.' From it all this sprang.

questions.query: When the Self alone is all this, how could one see another?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution

questions.query: What are the higher and the lower knowledge in the Mundaka Upanishad?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: Two kinds of knowledge must be known, this is what all who know Brahman tell us, the higher and the lower knowledge.

questions.query: What becomes of one who knows the highest Brahman?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: He who knows that highest Brahman, becomes even Brahman.

questions.query: What did Bhrigu finally perceive Brahman to be?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: He perceived that bliss is Brahman, for from bliss these beings are born; by bliss, when born, they live; into bliss they enter at their death.

questions.query: What does the Kena Upanishad say about Brahman and speech?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 1 (1879) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: by which speech is expressed, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.

questions.query: What happens to one who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 1 (1879) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: And he who beholds all beings in the Self, and the Self in all beings, he never turns away from it .

questions.query: Where does an Upanishad call nature maya and the great Lord the mayin?

gold.edition: Max Müller, SBE 15 (1884) · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: Know then Prakriti (nature) is Maya (art), and the great Lord the Mayin (maker); the whole world is filled with what are his members.

questions.query: Is the Self ever born or does it die, according to the Gita?

gold.edition: Swarupananda 1909 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
sections: Second Chapter. The Way of Knowledge
gold.quote: This in never born, nor does It die.

questions.query: Does the Gita say we have a right to the fruits of our work?

gold.edition: Swarupananda 1909 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
sections: Second Chapter. The Way of Knowledge
gold.quote: Thy right is to work only; but never to the fruits thereof.

questions.query: What does the Gita teach about the unreal and the real?

gold.edition: Swarupananda 1909 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
sections: Second Chapter. The Way of Knowledge
gold.quote: The unreal never is.

questions.query: How are actions burnt by the fire of knowledge?

gold.edition: Swarupananda 1909 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
sections: Fourth Chapter. The Way of Renunciation of Action in Knowledge
gold.quote: Whose undertakings are all devoid of plan and desire for results, and whose actions are burnt by the fire of knowledge, him, the sages call wise.

questions.query: What are the field and the knower of the field?

gold.edition: Swarupananda 1909 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
sections: Thirteenth Chapter. The Discrimination of the Kshetra and the Kshetrajna
gold.quote: This body, O son of Kunti, is called Kshetra, and he who knows it is called Kshetrajna by those who know of them (Kshetra and Kshetrajna).

questions.query: Is knowledge the only direct means to liberation in the Knowledge of Self?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: Compared with all other means, knowledge is the only direct means to liberation.

questions.query: What knowledge arising from 'That thou art' leads to liberation?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: The knowledge relating to the identity of the individual soul and the Supreme Self that arises from texts like "That thou art," is the means to liberation.

questions.query: How is the relation of the Self to objects like the rope and the serpent?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: Its relation to them as (subject and) object is (illusory) like the relation of rope, etc., to serpent, etc.

questions.query: How does the hymn to Dakshinamurti describe the universe as a reflection in a mirror?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: the universe as existing outside Himself although (more truly) it exists within Himself like the reflection of a city in a mirror

questions.query: What kind of enquiry does Direct Realisation recommend, such as 'Who am I?'

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: "Who am I? How was this (universe) born? Who is its maker? What is its material cause?" This is the kind of enquiry referred to above.

questions.query: How does the real seeker of liberation live while walking, sitting and sleeping?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: Feeling, while going about, that he is a wave of the ocean of the self

questions.query: What alone remains in deep sleep according to the Ten-versed Hymn?

gold.edition: Venkataramanan 1921, works attributed to Sankaracharya · Sacred Texts plain-text
gold.quote: I am He that alone remains in deep sleep, the secondless, uncontradictable  attributeless Bliss (Siva).

questions.query: What does the Kaivalya Upanishad say the witness is, other than enjoyer and enjoyed?

gold.edition: Narayanasvami Aiyar 1914 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: I am that Sadas'iva, (or the eternal happiness) who is other than the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the enjoyment in the three seats (or bodies), and who is witness and Chinmatra.

questions.query: When does the word maya first appear in the Upanishads, according to Barnett?

questions.query: In the Advaita-Makaranda, why is the Self called the Light that is everywhere?

gold.edition: Barnett 1911 · Sacred Texts plain-text distribution
gold.quote: I am the Light, and therefore am everywhere.

questions.query: How does Shankara define superimposition (adhyasa)?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: The apparent presentation, in the form of remembrance, to consciousness of something previously observed, in some other thing.

questions.query: What must precede the enquiry into Brahman according to Shankara?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: the antecedent conditions are the discrimination of what is eternal and what is non-eternal; the renunciation of all desire to enjoy the fruit (of one's actions) both here and hereafter; the acquirement of tranquillity, self-restraint, and the other means, and the desire of final release.

questions.query: What does Shankara say learned men call Nescience and knowledge?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: This superimposition thus defined, learned men consider to be Nescience (avidyâ), and the ascertainment of the true nature of that which is (the Self) by means of the discrimination of that (which is superimposed on the Self), they call knowledge (vidyâ).

questions.query: Why is release not a fruit of action according to Shankara?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: All which passages establish the fact that so-called release differs from all the fruits of action, and is an eternally and essentially disembodied state.

questions.query: How does the second sutra define Brahman?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: 2. (Brahman is that) from which the origin, &c. (i.e. the origin, subsistence, and dissolution) of this (world proceed).

questions.query: Why does Shankara say Brahman creates without any purpose, as sport?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: but proceed from mere sportfulness, as, for instance, their recreations in places of amusement.

questions.query: How does Shankara use the example of clay for cause and effect?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: if there is known a lump of clay which really and truly is nothing but clay, there are known thereby likewise all things made of clay

questions.query: What happens to earlier and later sins when Brahman is attained, according to Shankara?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: the non-clinging and the destruction of later and earlier sins; this being declared (by scripture).

questions.query: Does Shankara hold that Brahman is absolutely devoid of all difference?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: we must decide in favour of that according to which Brahma is absolutely devoid of all difference, not in favour of the opposite one.

questions.query: Why do released souls not enter new courses of existence, according to Shankara?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 34 (scan of 1904 printing) and 38 (1896) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: The existence of such a causal potentiality renders it moreover possible that the released souls should not enter on new courses of existence, as it is destroyed by perfect knowledge.

questions.query: How does Ramanuja describe the world as the body of Brahman?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
sections: Nor do Smriti and Purâna teach such a doctrine
gold.quote: owing to which the world is the body of Brahman, and Brahman the Self of the world.

questions.query: Why does Ramanuja say Nescience cannot exist in pure knowledge without a knowing subject?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
sections: The view that the conscious subject is something unreal, due to the ahamkâra, cannot be maintained
gold.quote: In pure knowledge where there is no knowing subject and no object of knowledge--the so-called 'witnessing' principle (sâkshin)--Nescience cannot exist.

questions.query: Are the experiences of dreams unreal, according to Ramanuja?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
sections: In cases of Scripture conflicting with Perception, Scripture is not stronger. The True cannot be known through the Untrue
gold.quote: The conscious states experienced in dreams are not unreal; it is only their objects that are false

questions.query: In Ramanuja's Great Purvapaksha, what does the opponent hold to be real?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: non-differenced pure intelligence is real, while everything else is false.

questions.query: Why does Ramanuja deny any proof of a substance free from all difference?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
sections: There is no proof of non-differenced substance
gold.quote: for all means of right knowledge have for their object things affected with difference.

questions.query: Why is plurality not unreal, according to Ramanuja?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: But jars, pieces of cloth and the like, do not contradict one another, since they are separate in place and time.

questions.query: How does Ramanuja's opening invocation describe Brahman's creation of the universe?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: who in sport produces, sustains, and reabsorbs the entire Universe

questions.query: Does the released soul enter into real union with the highest Self, according to Ramanuja?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
sections: Nor do Smriti and Purâna teach such a doctrine
gold.quote: It is false to maintain that the individual Self and the highest Self enter into real union; for one substance cannot pass over into the nature of another substance.' Accordingly the Bhagavad Gîtâ declares that the released soul attains only the same attributes as the highest Self.

questions.query: How does Ramanuja distinguish Brahman's intelligence from that of released souls?

gold.edition: Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) · Sacred Texts HTML
gold.quote: thus distinguishes Brahman from the released souls whose intelligence is sometimes in a contracted state.
